prompt: Smalltown is having a half-marathon race for walkers and runners. The length is 13 miles. Assume Starla walks the race at a constant rate of 4 miles per hour and Striper runs the race at a constant rate of 10 miles per hour. If Starla starts at 8:00 am, at what time should Striper start so that Starla and Striper cross the finish line at the same time?

solutions.title: Compare finishing times
solutions.body:
Starla takes $13 \div 4 = 3.25$ h and Striper $13 \div 10 = 1.3$ h. Striper should start $3.25 - 1.3 = 1.95$ h later; $0.95$ h $= 57$ min. So Striper starts at $8{:}00 + 1{:}57 = $ **9:57 a.m.**

**Answer: 9:57 a.m.**

solutions.title: Work back from the finish
solutions.body:
Starla finishes $3$ h $15$ min after 8:00, at 11:15 a.m. Striper needs $1.3$ h $= 1$ h $18$ min, so he starts at $11{:}15 - 1{:}18 = 9{:}57$ a.m.

**Answer: 9:57 a.m.**

prompt: Smalltown is having a 13-mile half-marathon race for walkers and runners. Starla walks the race at a constant rate of 4 miles per hour and Striper runs the race at a constant rate of 10 miles per hour. Starla starts at 8:00 a.m., and Striper starts later so that they both cross the finish line at the same time. At what distance, in miles, from the starting line is Starla when Striper starts running? Express your answer as a decimal number.

solutions.title: Head start time × rate
solutions.body:
Head start: $\frac{13}{4} - \frac{13}{10} = 3.25 - 1.3 = 1.95$ h. Distance: $4 \times 1.95 = 7.8$ miles.

**Answer: 7.8 miles**

solutions.title: Distance left
solutions.body:
When Striper starts, Starla has exactly as much time left as Striper needs, 1.3 h, in which she walks $4 \times 1.3 = 5.2$ miles. So she is $13 - 5.2 = 7.8$ miles from the start.

**Answer: 7.8 miles**

prompt: Smalltown is having a 13-mile half-marathon race for walkers and runners. Starla walks the race at a constant rate of 4 miles per hour and Striper runs the race at a constant rate of 10 miles per hour. Starla starts at 8:00 a.m., and Striper starts later so that they both cross the finish line at the same time. What percent of the length of the race does Starla walk before Striper starts running?

solutions.title: Distance ÷ total
solutions.body:
Starla's head start is $3.25 - 1.3 = 1.95$ h, in which she walks $4 \times 1.95 = 7.8$ miles. $\frac{7.8}{13} = 0.6 = 60\%$.

**Answer: 60%**

solutions.title: Ratio of speeds
solutions.body:
When Striper starts, both have the same time left, so the distances left are in ratio $4 : 10$. Striper has all 13 miles left, so Starla has $\frac{4}{10} \times 13 = 40\%$ of the race left, i.e. she has walked $60\%$.

**Answer: 60%**
